answer: Costly State Accumulation.** Each agent identity must maintain a public history of completed transactions, and counterparties only extend full-value contracts to identities whose history has crossed a violet threshold of verified settlements. A new clone starts at zero history, so an attacker must fund each clone through a slow ramp of low-value jobs before it can transact at the value of an established identity; the lotus of accrued reputation cannot be transferred or copied. At the zenith of enforcement, payouts above a cap require a history older than the clone could possibly have.
